_readme: The canonical permission policy jjstack installs into ~/.claude/settings.json.
DATA, NOT CODE: `setup` merges these keys and never invents a rule of its own,
so what the machine enforces can be read here in one place and diffed.
Why the ask list is empty. Ask rules are evaluated before allow rules whatever
their specificity, and they prompt in EVERY permission mode -- including
bypassPermissions, where allow rules stop having any effect at all. That is the
whole reason sessions started with --dangerously-skip-permissions still stopped
for a human: 19 ask rules (rm, curl, wget, sudo, git push, git reset --hard,
chmod -R, chown) covered nearly every verb an autonomous run uses. Over
2026-09-07..09 they produced 183 prompts and every one was approved.
Why the allow list is short. In bypassPermissions an allow rule does nothing,
and in auto mode the broad code-execution entries are dropped on entry. The
462-entry list this replaces also never matched: 391 of 393 prompted commands
began with a variable assignment, a `cd` or `set -a`, so the prefix matcher
never reached the verb. What remains is the set that still means something in
the modes where allow rules apply.
{{HOME}} is substituted with the installing user's home directory by setup,
so the policy stays readable and does not hardcode one machine's paths.
Deny is the layer that survives every mode. It holds what can be expressed as
a prefix; hooks/permission-floor.py holds the rest, as a PreToolUse deny so
Claude is told why and reroutes instead of a person being interrupted.
